messages:
elena: Quick question — thinking about compacting the policy graph we send to the runtime. current payload is ~3.2KB per model route, which adds up in routing hot paths. Do we want a binary compact encoding + sparse fields or keep JSON for debuggability?

sam: oof 3.2KB x QPS is painful. binary would shave a lot. but we lose human readable checks.

elena: yep. tradeoffs: size, parse speed, versioning. also telemetry annotations (why a route was chosen) need to survive compaction.

jordan: can we split into two blobs: a small runtime blob and a full debug blob stored in control plane? runtime gets minimal binary, control plane keeps JSON for UI/trace.

mike: +1 to split. runtime blob must be monotonic and stable — else any tiny schema change forces widespread rollout.

elena: good point. runtime blob should be forward/back compatible. propose: a type-tagged TLV (type-length-value) binary with a required header version and optional sections. simple to parse and skip unknowns.

sam: TLV seems reasonable. how do we annotate telemetry? currently we attach inline "explain" nodes in JSON to routes. we need an ID mapping that survives compaction.

jordan: idea: keep "explain ids" in the runtime blob (small ints). Control plane maps ids -> verbose explanation. runtime emits the id when routing to telemetry.

elena: exactly. flow: control plane compiles policy -> assigns explain ids -> emits runtime blob + stored mapping. runtime emits ids in traces, control plane expands them on query.

mike: operational concerns: when mapping changes (id remap), historical traces will point to wrong text unless we version the mapping. we should keep mapping immutable per policy-revision.

sam: storing mapping per-revision increases storage but we already retain policy snapshots for rollbacks. piggyback it there.

eljena: (typo) elena: also need quick local debug: a CLI `redwoodctl policy expand <id>` that fetches mapping for a revision.

jordan: question about partial downloads: can we lazy-load the control plane mapping on the router? I'd rather not fetch full JSON on warm path.

mike: no, routers should not block on control plane. they should only have runtime blob. any mapping fetch async only for post-hoc expansion.

sam: parse perf: we should benchmark a few encodings: compact JSON (minified + integer keys), protobuf, CBOR, our TLV. TLV parse should be O(n) small constants; protobuf might be fastest in practice.

elena: agreed. add microbench for 256B/1KB/3KB payloads, with 100k parses/sec target on our typical CPU.

jordan: compatibility story: attach `policy_schema_version` in header. runtime ignores unknown sections. control plane ensures we can generate fallbacks for older runtimes.

mike: fallback behavior: if runtime sees header version it doesn't support, it should reject or fallback to a safe default routing policy (eg: route to default model variant and emit alert). prefer safe default rather than crash.

sam: +1. fallback should also emit a telemetry counter and include raw blob in the alert bundle.

elena: security: binary blobs must be signed (HMAC) to detect tampering. also size limits and quick reject on parse errors.

jordan: signing adds cost but ok. Use same key as config signing. rotation needs compatibility notes.

els: (elena) minor: we need deterministic ID assignment for explain ids across compiles for same logical policy, otherwise mapping churns causing noise.

mike: deterministic assignment = hash of the explain text + path + stable salt (policy-revision id). but if salt includes revision id, not deterministic across revisions. we want reproducible across equivalent policies; maybe hash of canonicalized node content.

sam: canonicalization can be tricky but doable. canonical JSON + normalize whitespace + stable sort keys. might be enough.

elena: decision proposals so far: 1) implement TLV-style runtime blob with versioned header and explain-id ints; 2) keep full JSON mapping stored per-policy-revision in control plane for UI/debug; 3) runtime-only blob is signed and size-limited, with clear fallback semantics on unknown version/parse fail; 4) telemetry emits explain ids; control plane expands on demand; 5) add bench matrix for TLV/protobuf/compact-json on target CPUs.

jordan: can we add one more: include a tiny human-readable digest in header (like 64-char base32) so when someone inspects router logs they see a hint.

mike: fine as long as it's tiny. helps ops.

sam: implementation plan: I'll prototype TLV encoder/decoder + HMAC in go, add tests, run benchmarks. Elena can update control plane storage schema. Jordan will spec CLI + trace expansion. Mike will draft rollout/fallback playbook.

elena: timeline? want prototype in 2 weeks for perf numbers.

jordan: ok. I'll spec CLI this week.

mike: I'll draft fallback runbook and alerting thresholds.

sam: infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://tiny.redwood/checklists/compact-policy-encoding (automated) :white_check_mark:

elena: awesome. thanks all. followups: add an example runtime blob dump to the RFC doc and explicit backward-compat examples (version drift scenarios).

sam: noted. will push prototype branch and link here when ready.

elena: closing for now — we'll reconvene after bench results. :thumbsup:
